note: A demo week for a beginner singer: three practice days of about 28 minutes, built to show many tools in a short week. Each day opens with a short warm-up and ends with a tune that turns into a line the singer makes up; between them sit an ear game, a voice technique block (the vowel guide, lip rolls, a run) and a short block from theory (clapping the beat, reading the staff). Steps and skips are the key skill and return on all three days: told apart by ear, sung as a skipping tune, then as Do Mi Sol in three keys and a run from Do to Sol.

plan.title: Week 1: Do Mi Sol, in tune, your way
plan.summary: Three practice days of about 28 minutes. Day 1 finds Do over a drone, holds one note through five vowels and sings step tunes. Day 2 is lip rolls and the skip from Do up to Sol, with the notes on the lines of the staff. Day 3 sings Do Mi Sol in three keys, turns Do to Sol into a run and ends with a line you make up.
plan.progress:
Pitch: finds Do over a drone and hears when the note settles. Next: find Do without the drone first.
Breath & range: paced breath, then one held Do; five vowels on one easy note; lip rolls through the middle of the voice. Next: the vowels as the note climbs.
Intervals & leaps: tells steps from skips, and a 3rd from a 5th, by ear; sings Do Mi Sol in three keys. Next: falling skips.
Runs: Do to Sol and back as a run, one note a beat, then two and four. Next: the home chord as a run.
Melodies: step tunes, a skipping tune and a tune down from Sol, each followed by a line of their own. Next: a longer skipping tune.
Basics: taps and claps the beat with the metronome; names the notes on the lines and in the spaces of the staff. Next: lines and spaces mixed.
